verdict.rationale: Semgrep Secrets is documented as scanning code for exposed API keys, passwords and other credentials, and it validates whether found secrets are live, so scanning the current repository is covered. Nothing in the evidence shows scanning of full git history: the pre-commit hook only stops new secrets from entering history and does not scan past commits. missing for 10: documented scanning of full git history/past commits, independent or hands-on corroboration of secret-detection accuracy.

support.subject: As a developer, I can scan a repository and its full git history for hardcoded secrets and credentials

citations.quote: Semgrep Secrets scans code to detect exposed API keys, passwords, and other credentials.
valid secrets are those that have been tested against a web service and confirmed to successfully grant resources or authentication.
This is helpful in preventing secrets and security issues from leaking into your Git history.
